newsitem.title: ITALY: TENNIS-ATP CHIEF PROPOSES RANKINGS SYSTEM CHANGE.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-ATP CHIEF PROPOSES RANKINGS SYSTEM CHANGE.

text.p: Mark Miles, the chief executive of the ATP tennis tour, said on Sunday he would propose major changes to the men's world ranking system which may come into effect by 2000.
At a news conference before the Italian Open men's final, Miles said the proposals would be coupled with already-anounced plans to drop one or two tournaments from the tour's Super 9 events.

The proposed system would calculate players' positions by adding up points from their performances in the reduced number of Super 9 events, the four Grand Slams and their best results in a handful of smaller events.
"It would be easier for fans to understand," Miles said.
Under the present system, players count only their best 14 results from any of the tournaments in which they have competed over the previous 52 weeks.
Miles said the new system would compel players to give 100 percent at all the tour's major events.
"It would limit the extent to which players might not play so well at the big events...and yet it would keep the incentive for players to play additional events," Miles said.
